chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
My father sold a piece of land to Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik for money, and he stipulated in the sale that he would pay the zakat on this money from himself for six years.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on paying zakat on money received from selling property?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the practical application of zakat on commercial assets, where Imam al-Baqir (AS) sold land to the Umayyad Caliph Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik and stipulated that he would personally pay the zakat on the proceeds for six years. This specific stipulation highlights the scholarly view that zakat is due on trade goods and capital, and it demonstrates the Imam's meticulous adherence to fiscal obligations even in transactions with the ruling authority. It serves as a key precedent for the obligation of zakat on wealth derived from sale, emphasizing the seller's responsibility to ensure the purification of the transaction's value.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Myasws fatherasws was sold a land by Suleyman Bin Abdul Malik for cash, so heasws stipulated in his sale that he would pay the due Zakāt on this wealth from him for six years’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
My father purchased a piece of land from Sulayman ibn ‘Abd al-Malik for a certain amount with a condition that he (Sulayman) will pay its Zakat for six years.’”
